title: The Plan of Salvation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The plan of salvation is God’s gracious redemptive purpose to save sinners through Jesus Christ. Salvation is not an emergency reaction to sin, but the fulfillment of God’s wise and merciful purpose.
summary: The plan of salvation is God’s gracious redemptive purpose to save sinners through Jesus Christ. Salvation is not an emergency reaction to sin, but the fulfillment of God’s wise and merciful purpose.
christFocus: Jesus Christ stands at the center of God’s saving plan. In Him, God fulfills His promises, redeems His people, defeats sin and death, and brings sinners into eternal life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible presents salvation as God’s work from beginning to end. God planned, promised, accomplished, applies, preserves, and completes salvation according to His grace.

This plan unfolds through Scripture. God promises redemption, calls a people, gives covenants, sends prophets, prepares the way, and finally sends His Son in the fullness of time.

The cross was not a defeat that God turned into good by surprise. Scripture teaches that Christ was delivered up according to God’s definite plan, while those who sinned remained responsible for their evil.

The plan of salvation gives believers confidence that God will finish what He began. The God who purposed salvation in Christ will bring His people safely to glory.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people think salvation depends on whether they can keep themselves close enough to God. This doctrine lifts the believer’s eyes from human instability to God’s eternal purpose in Christ.

The plan of salvation also guards the Gospel from being reduced to a random religious offer. God’s saving work is purposeful, wise, costly, and centered on Jesus from promise to fulfillment.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Trust the wisdom and faithfulness of God’s saving plan. Do not treat salvation as fragile, accidental, or dependent on your ability to hold everything together. Rest in Christ, obey Him, and live with confidence that God’s redemptive purpose will not fail.
